known_gaps: turning the customer's words into negotiation events (and dates into YYYY-MM-DD) is done by the dialogue model; offers, counters, dates, amounts, read-back, recording, notes and the close are code
callback window validity is decided by the dialogue model from code-computed window facts (not code)
identity: the dialogue model turns the customer's words into answer parts and events; a misheard part is sent to the bank as heard (the bank decides)

extra rule (stateful, stage opening): Identity must be confirmed only by 'yes', 'that's me', 'speaking' or the customer's own name; ask once more, then close not_reached/unclear. A customer question is answered first and the following ask counts as the second ask. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (computational, stage negotiate): Interpret 'next <weekday>' as the weekday in the following calendar week and 'this <weekday>' as the one in the current week, relative to now. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): A weekend day or holiday not after the deadline is replaced by an offer of the next business day; a date after the deadline is replaced by an offer of the deadline, and refusing that deadline counts as a flat refusal. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Floor offered only once after 'too much' or after a below-floor amount; refusing it is a flat refusal that uses a persuasion attempt. Never repeat an offer already refused. Customer-proposed dates/amounts are never refusals. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Persuasion attempts are counted per product (1 for early band, 2 for late band); when used up, the product ends refused. Each product starts at attempt 1 and the today-question is asked only once for all products. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Hardship (illness, death in the family, job loss): one sympathy sentence, no persuasion, offer support transfer; accept -> transfer support, decline -> hardship. Takes precedence over rules 30 and 41, but a date/amount the customer names is still recorded. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Corrections at the read-back step invalidate the confirmation; re-validate the new value and read back again. A recorded promise cannot be changed; refer to the mobile app. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) no add_note calls are made before or after; promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded; close as transferred with that transfer's reason even if a promise was recorded. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (computational, stage closing): Close reason with no recorded promise across products: paid if all notes are paid, else no_promise with the reason of the first product in get_account order whose note is not paid. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

If the run is meant for Brief A only, add_note must be disabled.)

unresolved conflict: Rule 45 vs rule 15 before verification: chose 'Both give the same result: close not_verified/declined on the second refusal before verification' (Rules agree in effect; rule 45 states the pre-verification outcome explicitly.)
